candidates.text:
If you are building an Applied AI team and are not sure where to begin:

Do:
- Hire Product Engineers
- Let them sit with your domain (Ops/Finance, etc)
- No middle manager (aka PM) translating requirements
- Map out the workflows. Redesign workflows for AI where necessary. Give the agent the capability and knowledge to execute. In most cases, a workflow becomes a skill
- A single engineer owns the whole dev lifecycle for a sub-domain
- Define your north star, and see if applying AI to the domain is getting you closer.

Don't:
- Try to automate a single workflow, start with a domain
- Build multi-agent + orchestration until it's really necessary. Get there organically. 

Remember, in 2026, building agents are simple. Don't reinvent anything. Use a framework such as Mastra or LangChain to get started.

candidates.text:
Ruby Justice Thelot on wearables, biohacking, and the rise of body optimization:

"The Fitbit is launched in 2007... That idea of a quantified self has been with us for like 20 years... I feel like it's only being fully realized now, 20 years later."

"Slowly, through proper product development and slow adoption, we're seeing more and more adults adopt wearables as a way to control, understand, and improve their bodies."

"An idea that I like a lot around this concept of quantification of the self is the idea of body futurism by Toby Shorin."

"He says, 'Once we've reached the limits of innovation in silicon, we turn the microscope towards ourself and try to optimize and innovate on the body.' And that's what he calls body futurism."

"When I think about these dashboards that people have on these apps, waking up, going to your longevity clinic, even something like Don't Die, this is body futurism."

"The idea that you can use the same tools we did to make amazing phones, amazing tech, and revolutionize our external world, now we're trying to revolutionize our corporeal world, our internal world, and our organs and whatnot."

@being_on_line

in the whole optimism as performative mantra many ppl often forget a very very simple truth which is that to understand the future you first have to be brutally realistic about the present (i.e. you cannot be optimistic about the present!)

to be good at this you need to understand the world as it actually exists, why it became this way, which incentives sustain it, & which forces are beginning to break it apart or cause it to change. then you need optimism about tomorrow. i’m not talking blind optimism (that’s foolish), but the ability to see what could exist once all of these forces fully play out.

this is why great investors for example are unusually good at holding both of these complex realities at once. clear realism about today & optimism about tomorrow. it’s more important than ever to dissect the present without sentimentality so you could place bets for tomorrow.

The premature optimization of splitting animation work onto another process has done lots of harm to iOS (and web). For a brief while things were slightly smoother, but in exchange we ended up with uninterruptible animations and layout glitches from introducing unsolvable concurrency problems, plus various patches on top that ultimately make the system actually slower than if we just did things cleanly on main thread (or had access to proper multithreading in userland). Most tasteful UX cannot be decoupled in a computer sciency way

Smooth animations in general are great but calcifying the rendering pipeline for a decade is a huge cost

candidates.text:
Thought Experiment:

What if AGI Becomes the Ultimate Midtwit?

It’s fun to imagine AGI scenarios: from super abundance to dystopian. 

But… what if AI gets progressively smarter with more data and compute…

…but never achieves Einstein / Newton level insight?

In other words, AGI becomes the ultimate midtwit. The midtwit to end all midtwits. 

In that world, we throw more and more compute and we get better and better execution, analysis, automation, task delegation — 

but no Steve Jobs, Elon Musk, or Travis like creative potential. 

No AI designed fusion reactors, no AI theory of quantum gravity,  no AI decoding of the Sumerian tablets. 

(No AI religions either.)

Instead, we get a world of steady incrementalism, and productivity growth. 

Intelligence becomes a utility on tap. 

In that world, AI does what you want when you want. 

The AI gives you the conventional wisdom every time. Perfectly. 

MidTwit AGI never achieves dramatic breakthrus, except by brute force, but is exceptional at engineering and technique. 

Humans are looking at abundance and apocalyptic scenarios and under-exploring MidTwit AGI outcome. 

Wouldn’t that be an ironic and funny conclusion?
candidates.author: Ram Ahluwalia CFA, Lumida
